query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys have reported densities of 1.46–6 g/cm3 and commonly contain solid solutions together with intermetallic compounds. Earlier induction-melted Al–Mg-rich alloys established this structural complexity but did not resolve subsequent transformation pathways. Compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd alloys showed region-dependent compression and corrosion performance, while studies of AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys associated Mg content with phase stability and multiple functional properties. Most prior work emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, leaving corrosion, high-temperature oxidation, and evolution from metastable states comparatively underexplored. Within the design constraint of density below 6 g/cm3 and the tendency for constituent-property differences to promote stable intermetallic compounds, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain how a non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy evolves and why that evolution changes its corrosion and high-temperature oxidation behavior? Specify an unnamed controlled comparison, predictions relative to the initial baseline, boundary conditions, supporting prior observations, and an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, rapid synthesis induces metastable, Mg‐rich microsegregations that, upon thermal exposure, transform into stable Mg-containing intermetallic compounds. This structural evolution promotes the formation of a dense, protective Mg-oxide scale during high-temperature oxidation while simultaneously creating localized galvanic cells that alter aqueous corrosion behavior.
generation.material_initial_state: A non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable microstructure containing Mg‐rich segregations and mixed phase (solid solution and incipient intermetallic) regions.
generation.intervention: Post-synthesis thermal aging (controlled annealing) to activate phase transformations.
generation.conditions: Using alloys constrained to densities below 6 g/cm3, processed via rapid solidification (non-equilibrium route); testing includes high-temperature oxidation in air and aqueous corrosion environments, with a controlled comparison to near-equilibrium processed analogs.
generation.structural_mediator: Metastable Mg‐rich segregations evolving into Mg-containing intermetallic compounds.
generation.mechanism: The non-equilibrium processing route creates local Mg enrichments at phase boundaries. During thermal aging, these segregations transform into intermetallic compounds that preferentially oxidize to form a coherent Mg-oxide layer at high temperatures. In corrosive aqueous environments, the chemical heterogeneity from these phase changes establishes localized galvanic differences affecting corrosion pathways.
generation.predicted_outcome: After thermal aging, the rapidly processed alloy will exhibit a more continuous and protective Mg-oxide scale during high-temperature oxidation compared to its as-synthesized state, while also showing altered corrosion behavior (e.g., increased localized corrosion due to galvanic cells) relative to both its initial state and near-equilibrium processed variants.
generation.baseline: The as-synthesized non-equilibrium alloy with retained metastable phases and an analog produced via near-equilibrium processing.
generation.boundary: Alloys must adhere to the density constraint (<6 g/cm3) and be produced using a rapid solidification method to ensure non-equilibrium conditions; thermal aging parameters must be set to activate phase transformation without inducing complete homogenization.
generation.uncertainty: The exact distribution and volume fraction of the metastable Mg-rich regions and their transformation kinetics are not precisely known, nor is the precise magnitude of the corrosion rate changes, making detailed quantification of the outcomes uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys: one using rapid non-equilibrium processing and one via near-equilibrium processing. Subject both sets to identical thermal aging treatments. Analyze post-aging microstructures, oxide scale formation after high-temperature oxidation tests, and assess corrosion behavior via standardized electrochemical tests.
measurements: Microstructural characterization (SEM, TEM, EDS) to monitor Mg-rich segregation and intermetallic formation
X-ray diffraction (XRD) to identify phase transformations
Surface analysis (XPS) to assess oxide scale composition and continuity after high-temperature oxidation
Electrochemical corrosion testing (potentiodynamic polarization and EIS) to detect galvanic effects and corrosion rates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If thermal aging does not lead to significant formation of Mg-containing intermetallic compounds and the predicted changes in high-temperature oxidation (i.e., formation of a protective Mg-oxide layer) and altered corrosion behavior (due to local galvanic cells) are not observed when compared to both the as-synthesized and near-equilibrium processed alloys, the hypothesis is falsified.
